title: Critical Discourse Analysis: Wodak and the Discourse-Historical Approach
short_description: Guidance for discourse-historical analysis with attention to nomination, predication, argumentation, perspectivization, intensification, mitigation, context, and interdiscursivity.

phases.title: Historical context
phases.description: Situate discourse in historical, institutional, political, and interdiscursive contexts.

phases.title: Discursive strategies
phases.description: Analyze nomination, predication, argumentation, perspectivization, and intensification or mitigation.

prompts: What historical context changes the interpretation?

concepts.description: A CDA approach that integrates textual analysis with historical and contextual reconstruction.
prompts: How does history shape this discourse?

concepts.description: Naming or referring to persons, groups, objects, or events.
Attributing qualities, characteristics, or evaluations to actors or phenomena.
Justifications, topoi, and reasoning patterns used to support claims.
Positioning speaker perspective, distance, involvement, or viewpoint.
Strengthening or weakening claims, evaluations, or responsibility.
The mixing or articulation of multiple discourses.

sources.apa: Reisigl, M., & Wodak, R. (2001). Discourse and discrimination: Rhetorics of racism and antisemitism. Routledge.
sources.note: Use for DHA concepts and discursive strategies.

sources.apa: Wodak, R., & Meyer, M. (Eds.). (2016). Methods of critical discourse studies (3rd ed.). SAGE.
sources.note: Use for CDA methods, DHA overview, and comparative methodological grounding.
